Learn dsOMOPClient

Build useful study tables while patient records stay on the server. This book teaches the released 2.10.4 native recipe API, one small step at a time. Every worked lesson includes executed code, real synthetic results and an exercise with its solution.

Explore what you can do with dsOMOP →

Start with chapter 0 →

Your path through the book

Chapter What you will do
0. Getting started Install and open a practice session
1. DataSHIELD and OMOP Understand what stays private
2. Connecting Attach a resource and use symbols
3. Exploring the CDM Read schema and safe counts
4. Vocabulary Find concepts and build sets
5. A first recipe Create education and cause columns
6. Events, windows and reducers Choose records, time and one-value summaries
7. Populations Define eligibility, episodes, new users and matching
8. Output formats Choose shapes, censoring and joins
9. Dates Use parts, periods, anchored ages and partial dates
10. Concepts as categories Translate, recode, rename and harmonise two sites
11. Reusable studies and verbs Bind parameters and use mutate/filter
12. Privacy Understand final release and refused columns
13. Visit walkthrough Combine offsets, dates and event rows
14. Verbal-autopsy capstone Combine answers, age, visit periods and cause
15. Working with lab values Reduce, convert and pool synthetic lab values
16. Longitudinal data Shape events, build risk sets and model repeated measures

The main lessons use one DataSHIELD connection at a time. GiBleed teaches the basics; Synthea27Nj supplies numeric labs. Both have synthetic people. A separately labelled 24-person test fixture supplies the colleague’s questionnaire examples. Chapter 10 includes a two-connection vocabulary harmonisation demonstration. Chapter 15 pools numeric summaries and a Gaussian model across disjoint synthetic sites. Reproduction and migration notes explain how the examples run and how older recipe conventions differ. The visit walkthrough and capstone retain their original URLs so earlier links continue to work.

Learn with real execution

The displayed results come from DSLite running the matching released server and client against the chapter’s stated synthetic dataset. The verbal-autopsy example uses the released native follow-up recipe, including exact age at death and calendar precision. The optional local Opal/GiBleed instructions explain the production-shaped connection route; GiBleed is a different dataset.

Read the book in order. Use the function reference when you need argument details. The older reference guides are retained for existing links and are not the book’s learning path. This is an OHDSI-inspired theme, not an OHDSI endorsement.
